brief: A 20 mm cube of 1018 steel. It must weigh no more than 50 g. It carries no load, so there is no load case.

intent.summary: A simple 20 mm cube to be made of 1018 steel, constrained by a maximum weight rather than any functional load.
stated: Shape is a cube, 20 mm per side
Must weigh no more than 50 g
Carries no load; no load case applies
implied: Since a maximum weight is specified alongside a nominal material, the user expects the stated geometry and material to be compatible with that weight limit
No load case implies no stress/strength analysis is required for this part
unstated: Whether the 20 mm dimension is exact/nominal or has a tolerance
Any functional purpose of the cube (e.g. counterweight, test coupon, fixture) that would explain why weight matters
Whether 'no load' also means no handling, assembly, or incidental mechanical stresses need to be considered
Whether the weight limit is a hard pass/fail spec or a target
Any required markings, identification, or traceability on the part
risk_signals: Internal inconsistency: a solid 20 mm cube of 1018 steel (density ~7.87 g/cm3) computes to roughly 63 g, which exceeds the stated 50 g maximum weight -- the stated geometry, material, and weight constraint cannot all be satisfied simultaneously as given, and this contradiction is not acknowledged in the brief

requirements.statement: The finished part shall weigh no more than 50 g.
Overall width (X) of the finished cube shall be 20 mm.
Overall depth (Y) of the finished cube shall be 20 mm.
Overall height (Z) of the finished cube shall be 20 mm.
The cube's side length shall be 20 mm.

assumptions.statement: 1018 steel is assumed to have its standard mill density of approximately 7.87 g/cm^3 for mass calculation purposes.
assumptions.rationale: No density was stated in the brief; 7.87 g/cm^3 is the conventional handbook value for 1018 cold-rolled steel.
assumptions.consequence_if_wrong: A different density value would shift the computed mass, but the underlying conflict between a solid 20 mm steel cube and a 50 g mass cap would remain regardless.

document.name: steel_cube_20mm
document.description: A solid 20 mm cube machined from 1018 cold-drawn steel, constrained by a maximum mass rather than any functional load.

parameters.description: Side length of the cube, used for all three axes

answer.rationale: The part is a single square prism, so it is a single primitive box feature with one parameter, cube_side, written three times in the size vector to guarantee X=Y=Z stay equal under any future change. No booleans or holes are needed since the brief describes an undrilled solid block; material is set to the specific grade steel_1018_cd as required, with density handled by the compiler's material table rather than an invented assumption.

note: A 20 mm cube of 1018 steel must weigh no more than 50 g; solid it weighs 63 g. The repairs first shrank it (taken back: it broke the cube's size) and then shelled it inside to a 3 mm skin, and the shelled cube passed every claim. `answer` is the first design, the solid cube; `shelled` is the repaired one.
